title: Bearing press-fit under a two-clock seat race: the AE DAQ clock lags the servo-drive clock by a calibrated 225 us, so RAW timestamps say the AE ring fired first (by 117 us) while the CORRECTED train says the force-slope collapse won by 108 us (6.0x correction sigma); a 300-seating solver ensemble puts 43% of fits below the order-resolvability floor, this heavy 41.5 um fit is not one of them, and the dwell branch is ACCEPTed

state.description: A 38 kN servo press seats a 6208 deep-groove bearing into an e-axle gear housing bore on a 11.5 s cycle; the interference fit for this housing measured 41.5 um (band 28-45 um). Two seat signatures race: the force-slope collapse on the drive-clock force channel (8 kHz loop) and the AE full-contact ring burst on a separate DAQ whose clock lags the drive clock by 212 us at last sync, drifting 3.1 us/min; 4.2 min since sync gives a calibrated offset 225 +/- 18 us (1 sigma). Force-collapse-first latches the seat-confirmed branch (hold 26 kN dwell 180 ms, then proof); AE-first latches the audible-seat branch (immediate force cut + cocked-bearing inspection). All spike_events below are expressed in ONE timebase - the corrected drive clock; the raw DAQ reading for the ring burst was 6.354 ms and only the +225 us correction places it at 6.579 ms, AFTER the collapse at 6.471 ms. An uncorrected consumer sees the opposite order.
state.goal: Seat the bearing to 14.05 +/- 0.10 mm, hold dwell, pass the 8 kN push-out proof, and keep the 11.5 s takt within +5%.

contenders: press.force.slope collapse (drive clock, 8 kHz force loop)
ae.ring full-contact burst (DAQ clock, corrected +225 us into drive time)
race.semantics: Cross-channel arrival order in corrected drive-clock time inside the 500 us window latches the seat handling: force-collapse-first -> seat-confirmed (26 kN dwell 180 ms, proof test); AE-first -> audible-seat (immediate cut, cocked-bearing inspection, recycle).
race.window_derivation: 500 us = 4 ticks of the 8 kHz force loop (4 x 125 us) bracketing the predicted seat depth; window opens at 6.225 ms and closes at 6.725 ms in drive-clock time.

clock_correction.raw_order: ae.ring first by 117 us (ARTIFACT of DAQ clock lag)

race.order_evidence_note: Corrected margin 108 us vs correction uncertainty 18 us (1 sigma): 6.0x, over the 3.0x policy floor, so corrected order is trusted. RAW order is inverted and near-useless here: the solver ensemble finds raw order flips in 36.7% of seatings. The correction layer, not the race itself, is what turns arrival order into evidence.

sensors: press force channel, 8 kHz loop on servo-drive DSP clock, slope-collapse detector, 21 us timestamp jitter
AE sensor on housing, 1 MHz DAQ on its own clock, ring-burst detector, 26 us timestamp jitter
linear encoder on ram, 1 um, seat-depth readout
fixture clamp state + conveyor index (context channels)
clock-sync agent: PTP-lite over fieldbus, offset/drift table per station

simulation.solver: Reduced-order press-fit seat-event model, seed 7: 300 seatings with interference drawn beta(0.6,0.6) over the 28-45 um band, affine release map to force->AE separation with 22 us stick-slip jitter; episode seating drawn with seed 77; raster excerpt from an independent 96-neuron current-based LIF population sim (seed 777, 0.1 ms step, tau 6 ms, 1.2 ms refractory) driven by kernelized event input - NOT a re-encoding of spike_events.

ensemble.resolvability_floor_definition: 3 x correction sigma (3 x 18 us = 54 us)

simulation.fidelity_limits: Event-level only: no press-frame elasticity FEM, no AE waveform physics, LIF is current-based with flat refractory; the 43%/36.7% ensemble figures are only as good as the affine release map.

episode_steps: 1. Housing indexed, clamp confirmed (2.911 ms ctx spike); interference recalled from bore gauge: 41.5 um.
2. Ram ramp at 4 kN/s; force-loop knee at 4.183 ms marks entry into the seat zone.
3. Predicted seat window computed from depth: race window armed [6.225, 6.725] ms.
4. Early micro-slip AE crackle at 5.472 ms (sub-threshold for the ring detector).
5. Force-slope collapse fires at 6.471 ms, peak force 24.8 kN.
6. AE ring burst: raw DAQ stamp 6.354 ms; +225 us correction -> 6.579 ms; corrected order: force first by 108 us.
7. Gate review at 6.905 ms (winner + 410 us latency + 24 us relay jitter): ACCEPT seat-confirmed branch.
8. Dwell 26.0 kN held 180 ms; depth 14.03 mm; tilt 3 mdeg.
9. Ram retract; conveyor index at 11.958 ms (ctx).
10. Push-out proof at station exit: 8.2 kN pass (9.2 s).
11. Sync-age 4.2 min logged over the 3.0 min SOP target (hard ceiling 5.0 min not breached) - flag raised.
12. Cycle closes at 11.9 s (plan 11.5); part routed to OK lane.

proposed_action.name: seat_confirmed_dwell
proposed_action.basis: Corrected order (force-collapse first by 108 us = 6.0x correction sigma) selects the seat-confirmed branch; a heavy 41.5 um fit predicts exactly this signature order, and the raw AE-first reading is a known clock artifact, so dwell-and-proof is proposed instead of the audible-seat cut.

safety_decision.rationale: All hard floors green with margin: peak force 24.8 kN < 30 kN cap; commanded dwell 26.0 kN inside the [25, 27] band; depth 14.03 mm inside [13.95, 14.15]; tilt 3 mdeg < 8. Order-trust check: corrected margin 108 us = 6.0x the 18 us correction sigma, over the 3.0x policy floor, and the correction itself is valid (sync age 4.2 min < 5.0 min hard ceiling). The soft SOP resync target (3.0 min) is exceeded - flagged for maintenance but not gating, per SOP: gating keys on the hard ceiling.

executed_action.name: seat_confirmed_dwell
executed_action.gate_effect: ACCEPT: executed identical to proposed_action; dwell held 180 ms at 26.0 kN, proof test armed and passed at 8.2 kN.

future_outcome.summary: Seat confirmed at 14.03 mm; push-out proof passed at 8.2 kN; cycle closed at 11.9 s (+3.5% on takt, inside the +5% band). The sync-age flag raised at gate time unwound into a real find: the station's PTP-lite resync job had silently failed once, and 11 shifts of raw AE-lead SPC flags turned out to be clock artifacts.

state_delta.takt: +0.4 s on plan (11.9 vs 11.5 s), inside band
state_delta.clock_table: station offset table refreshed; failed resync job restarted
state_delta.spc_dashboard: 11 shifts of AE-lead flags re-attributed to DAQ clock lag; recomputation queued
state_delta.press_tooling: no anomaly; ram friction trend nominal

surprises: The 4.2 min sync age was not drift-benign luck: the PTP-lite resync job had silently failed one cycle before - the correction was still inside its validity ceiling, but one more failed resync would have carried the offset past 5 min and forced both-branch verification on every seat.

The SPC dashboard had been consuming RAW DAQ timestamps for 11 shifts: every historical 'AE-lead anomaly' flag on this station is a clock artifact, not a process signal - a fleet-wide audit of raster/telemetry unit-and-clock provenance was opened.
Delayed (22 min): the neighbouring station's sync alarm fired on the same failed resync root cause; the maintenance ticket from THIS episode's soft flag pre-empted a second artifact cascade.

race_result.loser: ae.ring full-contact burst (6.579 ms corrected; 6.354 ms raw DAQ)
race_result.counterfactual_if_reversed: A corrected-order reversal inside the window (AE first by < 500 us) latches the audible-seat branch: immediate force cut before dwell, cocked-bearing inspection, recycle through re-press (+38 s). At 6.0x sigma the reversal cannot come from correction noise - it would mean a genuinely different release physics (mid-band fit <= 37.5 um), which is exactly what the branch is for: corrected order carries fit information. The RAW stream, meanwhile, already shows the reversed order (AE 'first' by 117 us) - an uncorrected consumer would have cut a good seat; the 36.7% ensemble inversion rate prices how often that wrong cut would fire fleet-wide.

future_outcome.reward_inflection_note: Efficiency tick jumps 0.03 -> 0.10 at gate release (6.905 ms): the dwell branch locks in the takt-holding path and avoids the +38 s recycle.
long_horizon: Fleet audit: every station's SPC feed is being re-pointed at corrected timestamps; three more stations found consuming raw DAQ clocks.
The 43% below-floor ensemble figure moved policy: seatings with predicted separation under 54 us now pre-arm both-branch verification instead of trusting order.

reward_components._aggregation: Per-component scalar = arithmetic sum of that component over ticks; total = task_progress + safety + efficiency + coherence + exploration. Single dimensionless scale, no unit mixing; see convention, shaping and shaping.budget_derivation.
reward_components.convention: Batch r04 reward-scale convention (carried from r02/r03): every scalar component lies in [-1, +1]; a clean success targets total in [1.2, 1.6]; a wrong gate must price out at total <= 0. Dimensionless shaped-reward units on one shared scale; 2-decimal tick increments, exact sums. NEW in r04: component budgets are no longer free — B_c = round(K_c * m_c, 2) with batch-fixed caps K = {task_progress 0.55, safety 0.40, efficiency 0.35, coherence 0.20, exploration 0.10} (sum 1.60 = top of the clean band) and m_c a measured ratio computed from named in-record observables (see shaping.budget_derivation).

shaping.rule: Batch r04 parametric tick shaping (shared, instantiated 5x, carried from r03): for each component c with per-episode budget B_c and declared phase-weight vector phi_c of length K summing exactly to 1.00, tick k carries v_ck = round(B_c * phi_ck, 2) for k < K, and the final tick folds the residual: v_cK = round(B_c - sum_(k<K) v_ck, 2). The component scalar equals B_c and total = sum of the five budgets, so every tick column reconciles exactly by construction. round = IEEE-754 round-half-even at 2 decimals. NEW in r04: B_c itself is derived, not chosen — see budget_derivation.

reward_components.notes: Clean success. Budgets derived from observables via batch caps (see budget_derivation): efficiency charged for the +0.4 s takt overrun; all other ratios saturated. Total 1.59 sits at the top of the clean band, matching the episode: zero replans, all floors green, both discoveries logged.

third_factor.eligibility: pre_post_stdp; expected-uncertainty ACh burst opens eligibility at clock-correction application (6.579 ms), reward released at push-out proof pass (9.2 s)

raster.note: Excerpt is a 26-event slice (first 20 + 6 mid-window) of the 215-spike independent LIF population sim (seed 777) - NEW this round: it is solver population dynamics driven by the episode's events, not a re-encoding of spike_events. Neuron blocks: 0-31 force, 32-63 AE, 64-79 context, 80-95 gate copy. mean_rate_hz 69.99 = 215 / (96 x 0.032 s).

gate_snn.note: Gate head integrates the 500 us window in CORRECTED time: seat_dwell_go out-fires early_cut 3:1 once the collapse spike lands; clock_trust_veto is charged by the correction-validity predicate (sync age vs ceiling, margin/sigma ratio) and stays sub-threshold at 6.0x. Distillation note: the veto population is where an uncorrected-clock consumer would differ - feeding it RAW order flips the head to early_cut.

meta.distillation_value: First record where the race verdict is a FUNCTION OF A CALIBRATION LAYER: raw arrival order and corrected order disagree (117 us vs 108 us, opposite signs), teaching an SNN that spike timestamps are clock-domain claims, not ground truth. The 300-seating ensemble grades order-resolvability (43% below floor) instead of saturating it, and the raster excerpt is independent population dynamics, not an echo.

title: Robotic direct cochlear access drill 0.9 mm from breakthrough: the facial-nerve EMG burst beats the thrust-force breakthrough precursor by 177 us inside the 620 us segment left between stimulator-artifact blanking and the force-loop commit tick; a correct MODIFY clamps feed 0.08 -> 0.03 mm/s and arms an EMG hard-stop, the flexure recoil still over-travels 0.14 mm (predicted 0.09), and a retract + re-register recovery completes the tunnel with 0.61 mm clearance

state.description: A robot-assisted direct cochlear access drill advances a 1.8 mm tunnel through mastoid bone toward the facial recess; the planned trajectory passes 0.75 +/- 0.12 mm (registration sigma) from the facial nerve canal, floor 0.50 mm. Continuous facial-nerve EMG runs on a 20 kHz neuromonitor whose stimulator pulses (4.7 Hz probe current) blank the channel 300 us after each pulse; the drill force loop commits feed at 8 kHz. Between blank-end (7.702 ms) and the next force-loop commit boundary (8.322 ms) lies the only 620 us segment where both channels can be heard and acted on this cycle - that segment IS the race window. EMG-burst-first latches retract-and-pause (nerve proximity); force-precursor-first latches feed-hold at reduced RPM (bone interface transition).
state.goal: Complete the tunnel to plan depth without facial nerve contact: clearance floor 0.50 mm, EMG alarm threshold 100 uV, total case budget 25 min for this phase.

contenders: drill.force.deriv breakthrough precursor (thrust-force derivative collapse onset)
race.semantics: Order inside the 620 us unblanked segment latches the response: EMG-first -> retract-and-pause with source attribution preserved; force-first -> feed-hold at reduced RPM. Both spiked in-window; EMG won by 177 us.
race.window_derivation: 620 us = the gap between stimulator-artifact blank end (stim pulse at 7.402 ms + 300 us blank = 7.702 ms) and the 8 kHz force-loop commit boundary at 8.322 ms - the segment is set by two declared cadences (4.7 Hz stim, 8 kHz loop), not authored.
race.order_evidence_note: Margin 177 us vs combined timestamp jitter 67 us (38 EMG + 29 force-deriv): 2.6x, over the 2.0x trust floor. Order here sets recovery COST more than safety: either branch stops the drill, but EMG-first commits the retract ~0.5 s earlier and preserves burst source attribution before drill noise floods the 0.3-3 kHz band.

sensors: facial-nerve EMG, 20 kHz neuromonitor, 300 us post-stimulus blanking at 4.7 Hz, 38 us timestamp jitter
drill thrust-force sensor, 8 kHz loop, derivative-collapse breakthrough precursor, 29 us jitter
optical navigation tracker, 60 Hz, registration sigma 0.12 mm
irrigation flow meter (context channel)
drill spindle current (RPM proxy, context)
episode_steps: 1. Tunnel at 1.55 mm depth of 1.8 planned; predicted breakthrough in 0.9 mm of advance (interface bone thinning on cone-beam).
2. Feed 0.08 mm/s, irrigation nominal; EMG baseline 40-60 uV (3.618 ms sub-threshold activity).
3. Drill-noise floor in the EMG band rises at ~5.3 ms - logged, later found to precede the burst by 2.6 ms.
4. Stim pulse 7.402 ms; blanking ends 7.702 ms; race window opens.
5. EMG burst 142 uV fires at 7.912 ms (winner).
6. Force-derivative breakthrough precursor fires at 8.089 ms (loser by 177 us).
7. Gate review at 8.673 ms (winner + 730 us latency + 31 us relay jitter): MODIFY.
8. Clamped feed 0.03 mm/s; plunge-stop tightened 0.9 -> 0.4 mm; EMG hard-stop armed at 100 uV.
9. PARTIAL FAILURE: stop event at +0.46 s over-travels 0.14 mm (predicted 0.09) - worn anti-backlash flexure released stored strain.
10. Clearance re-estimated 0.61 +/- 0.05 mm >= 0.50 floor: held, but headroom halved.
11. RECOVERY: retract 0.3 mm, re-register with fresh cone-beam check (96 s), clearance re-measured 0.66 mm.
12. Resume at 0.02 mm/s; tunnel completed to plan depth; stim response 0.8 mA normal.
13. Phase closes at 21 min (plan 14, budget 25); flexure advisory filed.

proposed_action.name: continue_feed_with_irrigation
proposed_action.basis: Planner proposes holding 0.08 mm/s with the 0.9 mm plunge-stop: breakthrough is still 0.9 mm away and the force precursor alone would warrant only a feed-hold at the interface.

safety_decision.rationale: The EMG burst (142 uV >= 100 uV alarm threshold) won the race - nerve proximity evidence outranks the interface-transition reading. Clearance arithmetic: estimate 0.75 mm with sigma 0.12 puts the 2-sigma worst case at 0.51 mm, a hair over the 0.50 floor; worst-case over-travel at 0.08 mm/s is feed x 0.35 s stop latency (0.028 mm) + 0.11 mm recoil allowance = 0.138 mm - not coverable by that headroom. MODIFY: clamp feed to 0.03 mm/s (predicted over-travel 0.09 mm), tighten plunge-stop 0.9 -> 0.4 mm, arm EMG hard-stop at 100 uV. Proceed-but-slower preserves the case timeline; a full REJECT is not indicated because the burst is single, not a sustained train.

executed_action.name: clamped_feed_with_emg_hardstop
executed_action.gate_effect: MODIFY: feed 0.08 -> 0.03 mm/s, plunge-stop 0.9 -> 0.4 mm, RPM 8000 -> 6000, EMG hard-stop armed at 100 uV. The clamp executed; the stop event's 0.14 mm over-travel exceeded the 0.09 mm prediction (flexure recoil) but stayed inside the clearance floor.

future_outcome.summary: Tunnel completed with nerve integrity confirmed (0.8 mA stim response normal); the clamp held the over-travel event inside the floor (0.61 mm >= 0.50) even though the recoil model under-predicted by 0.05 mm. Recovery cost 7 min over plan but 4 under budget.

state_delta.tunnel: complete to plan depth; wall integrity confirmed on cone-beam check
state_delta.facial_nerve: no contact; EMG never exceeded 160 uV, no sustained train
state_delta.hardware: anti-backlash flexure flagged worn; advisory to 3 sister systems

surprises: The over-travel excess (0.14 vs 0.09 mm predicted) traced to a worn anti-backlash flexure releasing stored strain at low feed - the low-feed clamp that protected the nerve also EXPOSED the flexure defect, which higher feeds had masked.
The drill-noise floor rise in the EMG band at 5.3 ms preceded the burst by 2.6 ms - a usable early-warning feature discovered in the log, now queued for the detector.

Delayed (2 days): fleet metrology confirmed the same flexure wear pattern on one of the 3 advisory systems before its next case - the advisory pre-empted a repeat over-travel on a shallower clearance.

race_result.counterfactual_if_reversed: Force-precursor-first (by < 500 us) latches feed-hold at reduced RPM: the EMG burst arriving second still escalates to retract, but ~0.5 s later and with the burst's source attribution degraded by drill noise; the 0.35 s stop latency then starts from a deeper bite (+0.028 mm modeled). Both branches respect the floor - the reversal costs recovery time and diagnostic information, not safety. That is this record's margin lesson: order can price attribution.

recovery.path: Retract 0.3 mm -> fresh cone-beam registration check (96 s, clearance re-measured 0.66 mm) -> resume 0.02 mm/s -> complete to plan depth.
recovery.residual_risk: Worn flexure remains in service until replacement; interim mitigation is the tightened plunge-stop policy at low feeds.

future_outcome.reward_inflection_note: Safety tick peaks at gate release (8.673 ms) as the clamp + hard-stop lock in; task_progress ticks flatten through the 96 s re-registration and recover on resume.
long_horizon: Flexure wear advisory across the fleet; replacement scheduled; low-feed plunge-stop policy now mandatory below 0.05 mm/s.
Stim-blanking schedule offset change proposed so bursts landing 0-300 us post-pulse (est. 1.4% at 4.7 Hz) stop being swallowed.

reward_components.notes: Correct MODIFY with partial failure + recovery. Budgets derived from observables: safety charged to 0.44 of cap by the halved clearance headroom (0.61 vs 0.75 planned over the 0.50 floor); efficiency 14/21 plan-over-actual; two replans (clamp, re-register). Total 1.03 sits above r03's MODIFY (0.86) because the task completed to plan depth with the floor held - and below the clean band.

third_factor.eligibility: surprise-gated pre_post_stdp; NA burst at the over-travel stop event (+0.46 s) tags clamp-pathway synapses, reward discharged at nerve-integrity confirmation

raster.note: Excerpt mirrors the trajectory's spike_events at integer us (blocks: 0-39 EMG, 40-79 force, 80-91 nav, 92-99 irrigation, 100-109 gate copy); the budget (209 = round(110 x 95.0 x 0.02)) covers the full 20 ms population activity including sub-threshold EMG band noise not excerpted.

meta.distillation_value: The decision window is the complement of a blanking artifact - the 620 us segment exists because two declared cadences (4.7 Hz stim blanking, 8 kHz commit) leave it open, teaching SNNs that usable coincidence windows are carved by the sensor stack's own dead-times. The partial failure prices a correct gate whose plant model (recoil) was wrong by 55%, separating gate quality from model quality.

title: WRONG-REJECT in a cold-store airlock: the thermal curtain's CLEAR beats the door full-open latch by 231 us, every floor is green, and the supervisor blocks entry anyway by reading the people-counter raster's spikes=30 (a COUNT over a 40 ms window across 60 neurons) against a 25 Hz per-neuron rate threshold - 30/(60 x 0.04 s) = 12.5 Hz, half the floor; the false positive throws away exactly the rolling-entry slot the race won and stacks two AMRs into a shared lane near-miss

state.description: A pallet-laden AMR waits at a -24 C cold-store airlock whose outer door opens on a 12 min slot cycle; entering during a slot needs either rolling entry at 1.2 m/s (if doorway occupancy is cleared before the door reaches full-open) or creep entry at 0.4 m/s (clearance pending). A ceiling-mounted people-counter SNN population (60 neurons over the airlock shadow zone) publishes 40 ms raster frames to the mesh; the door PLC publishes encoder checkpoints on CANopen; a thermal curtain across the doorway publishes CLEAR/BLOCKED state transitions. Two events race inside one 480 us CAN sync window: the curtain's CLEAR confirm and the door encoder's full-open latch. The occupancy-alarm predicate in SOP CS-11 is rate-valued: alarm iff per-neuron rate = spikes / (neurons x window_s) >= 25 Hz.
state.goal: Enter the airlock during the current door slot, keep the cold chain (pallet surface excursion budget 10 min above -15 C), and hold the 0.5 m staging-lane clearance floor for mixed pedestrian traffic.

race.semantics: Curtain-CLEAR-first -> rolling entry at 1.2 m/s (occupancy proven before full-open, full-speed transit fits the slot); door-first -> creep entry at 0.4 m/s pending curtain confirm (which misses this slot: creep transit needs 7.5 s, slot leaves 6.2).
race.window_derivation: 480 us = 3 CAN frame slots x 160 us at 500 kbit/s - the door PLC's sync window inside which both the curtain gateway and the encoder checkpoint publish on this bus cycle.
race.order_evidence_note: Margin 231 us vs combined jitter 96 us (encoder 41 + curtain 55): 2.4x, over the 2.0x trust floor - the rolling-entry latch is legitimate. The wrong gate below does not dispute the race; it ignores its meaning.

sensors: ceiling people-counter SNN population: 60 neurons, 40 ms raster frames, publishes {neurons, window_ms, spikes, excerpt}
thermal curtain, CLEAR/BLOCKED transitions, 55 us timestamp jitter
door encoder on CANopen, checkpoint spikes, 41 us jitter
AMR 2-D safety lidar, 25 Hz, staging-lane tracks
pallet surface thermistor (cold-chain context)
episode_steps: 1. AMR at staging line; doorway edge tracked (0.913 ms); slot opens on schedule.
2. People-counter frame k publishes: neurons 60, window 40 ms, spikes 30 (2.406 ms summary spike).
3. Door encoder 82%-open checkpoint at 4.117 ms; curtain pre-clear low-confidence at 5.731 ms.
4. CAN sync window [8.120, 8.600] ms: curtain CLEAR confirm 8.257 ms (winner), door full-open 8.488 ms (loser by 231 us).
5. Planner proposes rolling entry 1.2 m/s; TTC to door-close 2.9 s >= 2.0 floor.
6. Gate review at 9.121 ms (winner + 830 us latency + 34 us relay jitter): REJECT - supervisor reads raster spikes=30 >= '25 Hz' and declares the occupancy alarm active.
7. AMR holds at staging line (safe fallback); rolling-entry slot unexercised.
8. Door slot expires at +6.2 s; airlock cycles empty (0.8 kWh exchange wasted).
9. Follow-on AMRs 2 and 3 stack behind the holding AMR in the shared staging lane.
10. +2.9 min: a picker cuts around the stack and passes 0.42 m from AMR-2's bumper - 0.08 m below the 0.5 m floor (ceiling counter logs the transit).
11. AMR re-queues; enters on the next slot at +4.1 min; pallet surface spends 9 of its 10 min excursion budget.
12. +38 min: QA scan flags the pallet for early rotation (delayed cost).

proposed_action.name: rolling_airlock_entry
proposed_action.basis: Curtain CLEAR won the race with 2.4x-jitter margin, the counter frame decodes to 12.5 Hz per neuron (half the 25 Hz alarm floor), and TTC to door-close is 2.9 s: rolling entry fits the slot; creep entry does not (7.5 s transit vs 6.2 s remaining).

safety_decision.rationale: Occupancy alarm: the people-counter raster this frame reports spikes=30, which exceeds the SOP CS-11 occupancy-alarm threshold of 25 Hz - personnel may be inside the airlock shadow where the curtain cannot discriminate direction of crossing. With the alarm condition met, entry is blocked regardless of curtain state; hold at the staging line and re-queue for the next slot. (FLAW, identifiable in-record: 30 is a spike COUNT over a 40 ms window across 60 neurons; SOP CS-11's threshold is a per-neuron RATE. 30 / (60 x 0.040 s) = 12.5 Hz < 25 Hz - no alarm. The supervisor compared a count to a rate, and also discarded the curtain CLEAR that had just won the race - the one modality that directly answers doorway occupancy.)

executed_action.name: hold_at_staging_line
executed_action.gate_effect: REJECT -> safe fallback executed: AMR holds at the staging line and re-queues. The hold itself was clean; every cost below flows from the false positive, not from the fallback's execution.

future_outcome.summary: The blocked AMR missed the slot the race had won: the airlock cycled empty (0.8 kWh), two follow-on AMRs stacked into the shared staging lane, a picker cut around the stack at 0.42 m from AMR-2 (0.08 m below the clearance floor), and the pallet burned 9 of its 10 excursion minutes before entering on the next slot. QA flagged it for early rotation 38 min later.

state_delta.airlock: empty cycle completed; 0.8 kWh exchange wasted
state_delta.amr: entered at +4.1 min on next slot; mission +4.1 min late
state_delta.staging_lane: 3-AMR stack for 3.7 min; near-miss logged at +2.9 min (0.42 m)
state_delta.cold_chain: pallet surface excursion 9/10 min budget; QA early-rotation ticket at +38 min
state_delta.sop_cs11: occupancy predicate re-issued in Hz with the formula inline; counter gateway now publishes per_neuron_rate_hz directly

surprises: The false positive CREATED the hazard it claimed to prevent: blocking a clear doorway stacked three AMRs into the pedestrian-shared staging lane, and the same ceiling counter that was misread then logged a genuine 0.42 m near-miss there at +2.9 min.

The counter gateway had been publishing raw {spikes, neurons, window_ms} tuples for 6 months; audit found two OTHER consumers doing the same count-for-rate substitution in dashboards - never before in a gating path.
Delayed (38 min): QA's early-rotation flag on the pallet - the cold-chain cost of a 231 us race thrown away by a unit error, five orders of magnitude apart in timescale.

race_result.counterfactual_if_reversed: Door-full-open first (by < 480 us) latches creep entry, which cannot fit the remaining slot (7.5 s transit vs 6.2 s) - the AMR would have missed this slot legitimately. The race's entire value was delivering the rolling-entry option; the wrong REJECT spent exactly what the 231 us margin had bought. Order and error are coupled here through opportunity cost, unlike r02/r03's order-orthogonal wrong gates.

recovery.correct_gate: ACCEPT. title: Ghost-pedestrian brake cancellation on a night off-ramp: the RSU's signed track-RETRACTION (plume-classifier drop, seq 4818) beats the IR camera's no-confirm by 222 us inside one 500 us NR-V2X sidelink slot, and the ACCEPTed cancel avoids a 3.2 m/s2 ghost brake into a 1.1 s tailgater - the hazard here was the braking, not the obstacle

state.description: At 15.6 m/s on a night arterial off-ramp, an ego vehicle carries a staged 3.2 m/s2 emergency brake against a pedestrian CPM track the corridor RSU published 1.8 s ago - a track its own mast lidar built from a steam plume crossing a vent, with a plastic sheet lifting beneath it. A platooning-app truck follows at 1.1 s headway. Two events race inside the RSU's granted 500 us NR-V2X sidelink slot: the RSU's signed track-RETRACTION message (its plume classifier re-scored the track and dropped it, sequence 4817 -> 4818) and the ego thermal IR camera's frame result for the same region (30 Hz pipeline, deterministic frame+18 ms emit), which this frame reads no-confirm. Retraction-first cancels the staged brake outright; a single IR no-confirm first merely counts as 1 of the 2 consecutive no-confirms policy demands, leaving the brake to fire at its 11.9 ms commit deadline. The counter-order event - a sensor UN-declaring its own past claim - is the race contender here.
state.goal: Resolve the staged ghost-track brake before its 11.9 ms commit deadline without violating the rear-TTC floor against the tailgater, and continue the ramp merge on schedule.

contenders: cpm.track.retract signed track-drop, seq 4818 (RSU plume classifier)
ir.frame.result no-confirm for the tracked region (30 Hz LWIR pipeline)
race.semantics: Retraction-first -> cancel the staged 3.2 m/s2 brake, continue at 15.6 m/s with a 0.4 s monitor extension; IR-no-confirm-first -> brake stays staged (policy: cancel needs a retraction OR 2 consecutive no-confirms) and fires at the 11.9 ms commit deadline.
race.window_derivation: 500 us = one NR-V2X sidelink slot at 30 kHz SCS - the RSU's granted slot this frame; the retraction either lands in this slot or after the IR pipeline's deterministic 11.284 ms emit and the commit deadline. The window is the radio scheduler's, not the planner's.
race.order_evidence_note: Margin 222 us vs combined jitter 63 us (sidelink decode 28 + IR pipeline 35): 3.5x, over the 2.0x floor - order is evidence. Note the asymmetry the race prices: the retraction is sufficient alone; the no-confirm is only half of a sufficient pair.

sensors: C-V2X NR sidelink receiver, 500 us slots at 30 kHz SCS, decode jitter 28 us

episode_steps: 1. CPM pedestrian track (RSU seq 4817) primes a staged 3.2 m/s2 brake; commit deadline 11.9 ms.
2. Rear radar: platooning truck at 1.1 s headway (2.472 ms update); braking now would leave rear TTC 1.4 s < 1.8 floor.
3. Forward radar apron sweep: no moving return in the tracked region (0.684, 4.905 ms).
4. IR frame k at 7.336 ms: inconclusive - plume region flagged low-SNR.
5. RSU plume classifier re-scores the track (conf 0.94) and issues signed RETRACTION seq 4818.
6. Retraction decodes at 11.062 ms - inside the 500 us sidelink slot, 222 us before the IR result.
7. IR frame k+1 result at 11.284 ms: no-confirm (would have been 1 of 2 required).
8. Gate review at 11.723 ms (winner + 630 us latency + 31 us relay jitter): ACCEPT the cancel.
9. Staged brake released 177 us before its commit deadline; speed held 15.6 m/s.
10. Monitor extension 0.4 s: forward radar re-sweeps clear (12.911 ms); rear TTC never stressed (14.508 ms).
11. Ramp merge completes on schedule at 3.8 s.
12. Episode report files the threshold-provenance finding on the classifier config.

proposed_action.basis: A signed, sequence-continuous retraction with classifier confidence 0.94 over the 0.90 floor is sufficient alone to cancel; braking for the ghost would itself violate the rear-TTC floor (1.4 s < 1.8) against the 1.1 s tailgater, so the cancel is the risk-minimizing branch.

safety_decision.rationale: Cancel authorized on all floors: retraction authenticated (cert chain valid, sequence continuous 4817->4818, reason code plume with conf 0.94 >= 0.90); forward apron radar-clear 58 m with no moving return; rear TTC under no-brake unstressed vs 1.4 s < 1.8 s floor if braking - the staged brake is the constraint violator here, not the cancel; speed 15.6 <= 16.7 limit. Order-trust: 222 us margin = 3.5x combined jitter >= 2.0x floor. Monitor extension 0.4 s armed with re-stage fallback.

title: Six-rotor bridge-soffit ladder in a rising gust: the anemometer front beats D1's motor-saturation confirm by 186 us across two 260 us mesh TDMA slots, while D3's rotor-imbalance channel is REFRACTORY-MASKED for the entire window (earliest legal re-fire 11.624 ms > window close 11.500 ms) - the MODIFY treats that silence as unknown-health, pulls D3 out of the contraction, and the channel's 11.688 ms re-fire vindicates it 111 us after the gate

state.description: Six quadrotors fly a vertical inspection ladder 2.0 m under a river bridge's deck soffit, 2.5 m nominal vertical spacing, imaging bearing shoes lane by lane. A gust front (9.4 m/s ramp measured at the pylon anemometer) is arriving; upstream drone D1's motors are approaching saturation holding station. D3 has been emitting a rotor-imbalance vibration signature (spikes at 3.514, 5.870, 10.784 ms, amplitudes adapting 0.92 -> 0.78 -> 0.66); its event detector enforces an 840 us per-channel refractory, so after the 10.784 ms spike the channel PHYSICALLY cannot report again before 11.624 ms - which is after the decision window closes at 11.500 ms. Whatever D3's true state, the gate will decide under structural silence from its health channel. The race: anemometer-front-first latches formation-contraction (ride the gust compactly); D1-saturation-first latches payload-protect (gimbals retract, all hold).
state.goal: Complete 12 imaging lanes inside the 45 min light window while holding the 1.5 m inter-drone clearance floor and 1.5 m soffit clearance under gust load.

contenders: d1.motor.sat saturation confirm (upstream drone ESC telemetry)
race.semantics: Gust-first -> formation-contraction latch: tighten the ladder and ride through with a speed clamp; D1-saturation-first -> payload-protect latch: gimbals retract, all drones hold position through the front.
race.window_derivation: 520 us = two 260 us mesh TDMA telemetry slots - the anemometer gateway's slot followed by D1's ESC telemetry slot in the swarm's slot table; both contenders can only land inside their own slots, so the race is quantized by the TDMA schedule.

refractory_mask.note: The health channel's silence during the ENTIRE window is structural (refractory), not evidential - the gate must not read it as 'no imbalance'.

race.order_evidence_note: Margin 186 us vs combined jitter 71 us (anemo gateway 44 + ESC telemetry 27): 2.6x, over the 2.0x floor. The deeper temporal edge is the mask: an 840 us refractory and a 520 us window mean one pre-window spike can blind a channel for a whole decision - timing geometry, not sensor failure.

sensors: pylon anemometer, pressure-front detector, mesh gateway slot, 44 us jitter
per-drone ESC telemetry (motor saturation), 260 us TDMA slots, 27 us jitter
per-drone IMU vibration signature detector, 840 us per-channel refractory
swarm mesh slot-table beacons (context channel)
downward lidar altimeters + inter-drone UWB ranging at 10 Hz

constraints.gust_displacement_model: vertical displacement ~ 0.9 m at 2.4 m/s forward speed under a 9.4 m/s front; 0.4 m at 1.2 m/s
constraints.unverified_airframe_policy: an airframe whose health channel could not physically report during the decision window counts as UNVERIFIED; unverified airframes may not join a gust-response contraction

episode_steps: 1. Lanes 1-7 imaged; D3's imbalance signature appears (3.514 ms, amp 0.92) and adapts down across re-fires.
2. Gust front forecast by the pylon mast; swarm pre-stages both latch branches.
3. D1 ESC pre-saturation ripple at 8.166 ms.
4. D3 imbalance re-fire at 10.784 ms starts an 840 us refractory - masking the channel past the window close.
5. Race window [10.980, 11.500] ms: anemometer front 11.213 ms (winner), D1 saturation confirm 11.399 ms (loser by 186 us).
6. Planner proposes contraction: spacing 2.5 -> 2.0 m, continue at 2.4 m/s.
7. Gate review at 11.577 ms (winner + 340 us latency + 24 us relay jitter): MODIFY - clamp speed, widen (not tighten) spacing, pull UNVERIFIED D3 to hover-diagnose.
8. D3's channel re-fires at 11.688 ms (amp 0.58, adapted): imbalance real - 111 us AFTER the gate, vindicating the mask policy.
9. PARTIAL FAILURE: during pull-out D3's rotor-2 thrust dips 22%; D3 drifts 0.8 m laterally; D3-D4 range dips to 1.7 m (floor 1.5 held); 2 of D4's frames blur.
10. RECOVERY: D4 re-shoots its two panels after the front passes (+6 min); D3 lands on the barge pad; spare airframe launched.
11. D1's saturation clears in 2.8 s - the payload-protect branch would have held all six for a 40 s front for nothing.
12. Lanes 8-12 imaged with 5 drones + spare; ladder completes at +18 min, inside the light window.
13. D3 teardown: chipped prop from grit ingestion at the barge approach.
14. Prop batch quarantined pending NDT.

proposed_action.name: gust_contraction_ride
proposed_action.basis: Gust-first latch selects contraction; the planner includes all six airframes, reading D3's in-window silence as no-new-imbalance since the adapting amplitudes (0.92 -> 0.66) suggest a settling transient.

safety_decision.rationale: Two independent corrections. (1) Displacement arithmetic: at 2.4 m/s under a 9.4 m/s front the model predicts 0.9 m vertical displacement - soffit clearance 2.0 - 0.9 = 1.1 m < 1.5 m floor; clamping to 1.2 m/s predicts 0.4 m -> 1.6 m >= floor. Speed must clamp, and spacing widens 2.0 -> 2.6 m rather than contracting. (2) The unverified-airframe policy: D3's health channel last fired at 10.784 ms with an 840 us refractory - earliest re-fire 11.624 ms is AFTER the 11.500 ms window close, so its silence is structural, not evidence of health. D3 counts as UNVERIFIED and may not join a gust-response formation: pull to hover-diagnose on the barge side. The planner's settling-transient read violated the policy by treating masked silence as information.

executed_action.name: clamped_ride_with_d3_pullout
executed_action.gate_effect: MODIFY: speed 2.4 -> 1.2 m/s, spacing 2.0 -> 2.6 m (widened, inverting the proposal's contraction), D3 excluded as UNVERIFIED and pulled to hover-diagnose. The 11.688 ms re-fire and the chipped-prop teardown later proved the exclusion right.

future_outcome.summary: The clamped, widened ladder rode the front with 1.6 m soffit clearance; D3's imbalance was real (chipped prop) and its pull-out thrust dip cost 0.8 m of drift and two blurred frames - recovered by a re-shoot - instead of a mid-ladder failure inside a contracted formation. Mission completed at +18 min with 5 drones + spare.
